name: Jehoiachin (son of Jehoiakim)
title: Judah's last king before the exile
summary: Jehoiachin was king of Judah for only three months before he was taken into exile in Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC. He spent 37 years in captivity before being released and honored by the Babylonian king Evil-Merodach. He is an important figure in Jesus' genealogy as mentioned in the Gospel of Matthew.

keyEvents.title: Becomes king over Judah
keyEvents.description: Jehoiachin became king at the age of eighteen and reigned for three months in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the Lord's sight.

keyEvents.title: Jerusalem besieged and Jehoiachin surrenders
keyEvents.description: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon besieged Jerusalem, and Jehoiachin surrendered to the king of Babylon along with his mother, his officials, and his leaders.

keyEvents.title: Exile to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Jeconiah was taken to Babylon along with the treasures of the royal house, the temple treasures, and all the leading men of Judah—ten thousand captives in total.

keyEvents.title: The Prophecy Concerning His Descendants
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah prophesied that Jeconiah (called Coniah) would be rejected and that none of his descendants would sit on David's throne to rule over Judah.

keyEvents.title: Release and Restoration in Babylon
keyEvents.description: After 37 years in captivity, Jeconiah was released by Evil-Merodach, the new king of Babylon, who showed him favor and gave him a place of honor among the kings of Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jesus' Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Jeconiah (called Jehoiachin) is mentioned in the genealogy in the Gospel of Matthew as one of Jesus' ancestors, demonstrating God's faithfulness to the Davidic covenant despite the exile.
